questions.question_text: Which of the following research methods is considered to have the highest credibility?

options.text: Case reports
Prospective studies
Cross-sectional studies
Retrospective studies
Case series

correct_answer.text: Prospective studies

correct_answers.text: Prospective studies

questions.explanation: Prospective studies are considered to have the highest credibility when compared to the other types of studies mentioned. The gold standards, however, are the randomized placebo-controlled trials.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is likely to be the best guide for evidence-based practice?

options.text: Randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trials
Cross-sectional studies
Retrospective studies
Meta-analysis of randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trials
Review articles

correct_answer.text: Meta-analysis of randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trials

correct_answers.text: Meta-analysis of randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trials

questions.explanation: Meta-analysis of a number of randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trials is considered to be the best possible guide for evidence-based practice. They are considered more effective than individual randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trials.

questions.question_text: In epidemiological studies, which of the following is not used as a method to compensate for confounding variables?

options.text: Recruitment
Standardization
Randomization
Matching
Modelling

correct_answer.text: Recruitment

correct_answers.text: Recruitment

questions.explanation: All the other four methods are commonly used to compensate for confounding variables such as age and sex.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements best explains the meaning of 'number needed to treat'?

options.text: It explains the benefit for treating a large number of people
It means that treating a minimum number of people can be of some benefit
It expresses the benefit of an active treatment over placebo
It expresses the benefit of placebo over an active treatment
None of the above

correct_answer.text: It expresses the benefit of an active treatment over placebo

correct_answers.text: It expresses the benefit of an active treatment over placebo

questions.explanation: The 'number needed to treat' expresses the benefit of an active treatment over placebo. It is not only useful in explaining the outcome of a trial but it can also be used while making individual treatment decisions.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements best describes the 'positive predictive value' of a screening instrument?

options.text: The proportion of positive results that are truly positive
The sum of all the positive results
The proportion of negative results that are truly negative
The sum of all negative results
None of the above

correct_answer.text: The proportion of positive results that are truly positive

correct_answers.text: The proportion of positive results that are truly positive

questions.explanation: The positive predictive value is the proportion of positive results that are truly positive. The negative predictive value is the proportion of negative results that are truly negative. Both positive and negative predictive values of screening instruments are expressed as percentages.

questions.question_text: The lifetime risk for a major depressive disorder in women in the Western world is:

options.text: One in two
One in four
One in six
One in eight
One in ten

correct_answer.text: One in four

correct_answers.text: One in four

questions.explanation: The lifetime risk for a major depressive disorder in Western countries for women is one in four; for men it is one in ten.

questions.question_text: What is the annual incidence of schizophrenia?

options.text: 1–2 per 100 000 population
5–10 per 100 000 population
10–20 per 100 000 population
100 per 100 000 population
200 per 100 000 population

correct_answer.text: 10–20 per 100 000 population

correct_answers.text: 10–20 per 100 000 population

questions.explanation: The annual incidence of schizophrenia worldwide is 10–20 per 100 000 population. Some studies have shown a higher annual incidence in some ethnic groups such as Afro-Caribbean immigrants in the UK.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true regarding suicide?

options.text: Suicide rates are highest in young women
Suicide rates are highest in young men
Suicide rates are highest in older women
Suicide rates are highest in older men
There is no age or gender difference in suicide rates

correct_answer.text: Suicide rates are highest in older men

correct_answers.text: Suicide rates are highest in older men

questions.explanation: Suicide rates are highest in older men. The risk is higher if they are unmarried or divorced.

questions.question_text: Epidemiologically, which of the following groups of people has a higher rate of schizophrenia than the general population?

options.text: Children with a biological parent suffering from schizophrenia
Children with a first-degree relative suffering from schizophrenia
Adopted children with a foster parent suffering from schizophrenia
Adopted children with a biological parent suffering from schizophrenia
Adopted children with a foster sibling suffering from schizophrenia

correct_answer.text: Children with a biological parent suffering from schizophrenia

correct_answers.text: Children with a biological parent suffering from schizophrenia

questions.explanation: Children brought up by a biological parent suffering from schizophrenia are likely to have a higher rate of schizophrenia than the general population.

questions.question_text: Incidence can be defined as:

options.text: The number of new cases of illness at a given point in time
The number of new cases occurring in a population over a designated period of time
The number of hospital admissions during a designated time period
The number of deaths during a designated time period
The number of beds occupied in a hospital over a designated period of time

correct_answer.text: The number of new cases occurring in a population over a designated period of time

correct_answers.text: The number of new cases occurring in a population over a designated period of time

questions.explanation: Incidence is a measure of the frequency with which an event, such as a new case of illness, occurs in a population over a designated period of time. The formula for calculating an incidence rate is as follows: Incidence rate ¼New cases occurring in a given time period Total population in a given time period/C210n

questions.question_text: Prevalence can be defined as:

options.text: The total number of new cases reported in a designated period of time
The total number of treated cases in a population in a designated period of time
All new and pre-existing cases during a given period of time in a population
The total number of resistant cases of an illness in a population
The total number of hospital admissions due to a particular disease in a given population

correct_answer.text: All new and pre-existing cases during a given period of time in a population

correct_answers.text: All new and pre-existing cases during a given period of time in a population

questions.explanation: Prevalence is the proportion of people in a population who have a particular disease (both new and existing cases) over a specified period of time.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not true about point prevalence?

options.text: It is a snapshot look at the population with regard to a particular disease
It is the number of people with a particular disease on a particular date
It includes both new and pre-existing cases
It is not similar to incidence
It is the number of people with a particular illness at any time during a specific time interval

correct_answer.text: It is the number of people with a particular illness at any time during a specific time interval

correct_answers.text: It is the number of people with a particular illness at any time during a specific time interval

questions.explanation: The number of people with a particular illness at any time during a particular time interval is period prevalence.

questions.question_text: In a population of 5000 people surveyed for psychosis, a prevalence rate of 7 per 1000 in 12 months was reported. What does it mean?

options.text: Seven new cases per 1000 population every year
Seven referrals to psychiatric services per 1000 population every year
A total of seven cases of psychosis per 1000 population every year
Seven treated cases of psychosis per 1000 population every year
Seven old cases of psychosis per 1000 population every year

correct_answer.text: A total of seven cases of psychosis per 1000 population every year

correct_answers.text: A total of seven cases of psychosis per 1000 population every year

questions.explanation: Prevalence is the total number of cases (both new and old) in a given population during a specified period of time.

questions.question_text: Suppose an epidemiological study of relapse of psychotic illness and cannabis use reports a relative risk of 4.41 in cannabis users. What does it mean?

options.text: The relapsed cases are 4.41 times more likely to have had exposure to cannabis
Those with exposure to cannabis are 4.41 times more likely to have a relapse
People smoking cannabis are 4.41 times more likely to develop psychosis
Banning the use of cannabis is likely to reduce the incidence of psychosis by 4.41 times
There is no increased risk of a relapse of psychosis in people using cannabis

correct_answer.text: Those with exposure to cannabis are 4.41 times more likely to have a relapse

correct_answers.text: Those with exposure to cannabis are 4.41 times more likely to have a relapse

questions.explanation: This report provides the relative risk of relapse of psychosis after exposure to cannabis. It means that there is a 4.41 times higher risk of relapse of psychosis in those exposed to cannabis.

questions.question_text: Suppose an epidemiological study looking at severe head injury and cognitive decline reports an odd ratio of 5.44 in the exposed population. What does this mean?

options.text: People with cognitive decline are 5.44 times more likely to have had a severe head injury compared with those without cognitive decline
People involved in severe head injuries are 5.44 times more likely to develop cognitive decline
Cognitive decline after a severe head injury is inevitable
Severe head injuries are the most common cause of cognitive decline
People who have suffered from a head injury more than five times will always develop cognitive decline

correct_answer.text: People involved in severe head injuries are 5.44 times more likely to develop cognitive decline

correct_answers.text: People involved in severe head injuries are 5.44 times more likely to develop cognitive decline

questions.explanation: The odds ratio of 5.44 means that the odds of people developing cognitive decline after a severe head injury is 5.44 times higher than the odds in the general population.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statements is not true regarding the reliability of an instrument?

options.text: It is concerned with the accuracy of its measurement
It is high if the rating of the same instrument by other raters is similar
It is high if its measurements accord with those of other instruments supposed to have the same function
It concerns the reliability of its measurements
It is high if the results are similar when the instrument is administered at two different time points

correct_answer.text: It is concerned with the accuracy of its measurement

correct_answers.text: It is concerned with the accuracy of its measurement

questions.explanation: The reliability of an instrument gives an idea of how consistent the results will be if the instrument was used by a number of people or at different time intervals. Sensitivity gives an idea of how accurate an instrument is.

questions.question_text: Which of the following measures is best suited to picking out the leading causes of death in a specific population?

options.text: Mortality rates
Crude death rate
Incidence
Proportional mortality
Prevalence

correct_answer.text: Proportional mortality

correct_answers.text: Proportional mortality

questions.explanation: Proportional mortality is described as a proportion of deaths in a specified population over a period of time attributable to different causes. Each cause is expressed as a percentage of all the deaths and the sum of the causes must add to 100%. For example, according to figures from the USA, in 1987, suicide was ranked eighth among the causes of mortality, with a proportionate mortality of 1.5%, which means that among all the deaths reported within the USA in 1987, 1.5% of those deaths were caused by suicide.

questions.question_text: The following formula can be used to calculate both incidence and prevalence for a specified time period: (X/Y)X10n, Which of the following determines the primary difference between incidence and prevalence?

options.text: X
Y
The time period
None of the above

correct_answer.text: X

correct_answers.text: X

questions.explanation: The primary difference between incidence and prevalence is in what cases are included in X. For incidence, X is restricted to new cases; for prevalence, X includes both new and pre-existing cases.

questions.question_text: An epidemiological study was conducted on two different types of cancers (A and B). It was found that the prevalence of cancer A was higher than that of cancer B but the incidence of both diseases was similar. Which of the following explanations could be responsible for these findings?

options.text: Patients recover more quickly from cancer A than from cancer B
Patients recover more quickly from cancer B than from cancer A
Patients die more quickly from cancer A than from cancer B
Patients with cancer A are not being treated properly
None of the above

correct_answer.text: Patients recover more quickly from cancer B than from cancer A

correct_answers.text: Patients recover more quickly from cancer B than from cancer A

questions.explanation: Prevalence is based on both incidence and duration. If the incidence of the two cancers is similar then the difference in prevalence must reflect a difference in duration. Since cancer A is more prevalent than cancer B, its duration must be longer than that of cancer B. The two possible explanations for cancer B being of shorter duration could be either rapid recovery or rapid mortality.

questions.question_text: To investigate the association between dementia and stroke, investigators conducted a case-control study of 100 cases (people with dementia) and 100 controls (people without dementia). Among the dementia cases, 50 had a history of stroke. Among those without dementia, 25 had a history of stroke. For this study, the odds ratio is:

options.text: It cannot be calculated from the given information

questions.explanation: The odds ratio for this case-controlled study can be calculated by arranging the data in the following 2 /C22 table Cases Controls Total Exposed A = 50 B = 25 75 Unexposed C = 50 D = 75 125 Total 100 100 200 Odds ratio = AD/BC = 50 /C275/25 /C250 = 3.0

questions.question_text: Which measure, relating to the epidemiology of schizophrenia, is the following equation likely to calculate? Number of patients in UK on 1 January 2010 Total population of UK on 1 January 2010¼?

options.text: Incidence rate
Attack rate
Person time rate
Period prevalence
Point prevalence

correct_answer.text: Point prevalence

correct_answers.text: Point prevalence

questions.explanation: The numerator includes pre-existing cases, so we know we are dealing with prevalence rather than incidence. Both numerator and denominator are measured at a point in time (1 January 2010) so it is point prevalence rather than period prevalence.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements are true regarding the use of psychiatric screening instruments in a general hospital setting, except:

options.text: They are used to detect uncommon syndromes
They should have cut-off scores based on sensitivity
They require normal distribution of scores
They include the CAGE questionnaire
They include the Geriatric Depression Scale

correct_answer.text: They are used to detect uncommon syndromes

correct_answers.text: They are used to detect uncommon syndromes

questions.explanation: Screening instruments are used to detect common syndromes such as depression, anxiety and alcohol abuse. They are not useful in detecting uncommon syndromes.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not true regarding rating scales in psychiatry?

options.text: Rating scales convert descriptive information into numerical data
The scores of rating scales cannot be used for inclusion or exclusion from a study
Rating scales can have cultural bias
The Brief Psychiatric Rating Scale (BPRS) measures positive symptoms
There are separate Hamilton rating scales for anxiety and depression

correct_answer.text: The scores of rating scales cannot be used for inclusion or exclusion from a study

correct_answers.text: The scores of rating scales cannot be used for inclusion or exclusion from a study

questions.explanation: The scores on a rating scale can be used to determine inclusion and exclusion from a study.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a commonly used epidemiological study design?

options.text: Case-control study
Cross-sectional cohort survey
Ecological study
Randomized controlled trial
Systematic review

correct_answer.text: Cross-sectional cohort survey

correct_answers.text: Cross-sectional cohort survey

questions.explanation: Cohort studies are longitudinal and not cross-sectional.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a possible source of bias in epidemiological studies?

options.text: The procedure of matching controls to individual cases
Use of a measurement of exposure not independent of presence of disease
Retrospective exposure assessment
Adequate selection of controls
Effort after meaning

correct_answer.text: Adequate selection of controls

correct_answers.text: Adequate selection of controls

questions.explanation: Adequate selection of controls will minimize the possibility of bias. Effort after meaning is the recall bias that can occur in ill people looking for an explanation for their illness.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements are true regarding confounding variables in epidemiological research, except:

options.text: They can be either a risk factor or a protective factor
They can be associated with both exposure and disease
They can be taken into account by introducing randomization in a study design
They are on the causal pathway between exposure and disease
They can be taken into account by introducing matching into a study design

correct_answer.text: They are on the causal pathway between exposure and disease

correct_answers.text: They are on the causal pathway between exposure and disease

questions.explanation: The confounding variables are not on the causal pathway between exposure and disease.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not true regarding case-control studies?

options.text: They are experimental studies
They compare a group of cases with a group of controls
They can indicate possible risk factors for an illness
Odds ratios can be estimated from these studies
They cannot by themselves prove causality

correct_answer.text: They are experimental studies

correct_answers.text: They are experimental studies

questions.explanation: Case-controlled studies are observational studies.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a rating scale for depression?

options.text: HRSD
BPRS
MADRS
BDI
HADS

correct_answer.text: BPRS

correct_answers.text: BPRS

questions.explanation: The BPRS (Brief Psychiatric Rating Scale) is used to measure positive symptoms in schizophrenia.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not true regarding confounding variables in epidemiological studies?

options.text: They can lead to a spurious association
They can be an independent risk factor for the disease
They can never be a protective factor for the disease
They can be adjusted by randomization
They can be adjusted by matching

correct_answer.text: They can never be a protective factor for the disease

correct_answers.text: They can never be a protective factor for the disease

questions.explanation: A confounder can either be an independent risk factor or a protective factor for the disease.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not true regarding reliability?

options.text: It implies diagnostic consistency
High reliability implies high validity
It relates to the agreement between tests done on different occasions
It relates to the agreement between raters
It can be estimated by assessing test–retest reliability

correct_answer.text: High reliability implies high validity

correct_answers.text: High reliability implies high validity

questions.explanation: High reliability does not necessarily imply high validity.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not true regarding validity?

options.text: The validity of diagnosis cannot be assessed by comparison with a gold standard
Criterion validity means how valid the diagnosis is when judged against one or more external validators
Face validity looks at whether the criteria used overtly relate to the diagnosis
Construct validity looks at the conceptual soundness of the diagnosis and its consistency with available data
Predictive validity looks at whether the diagnosis can be used to accurately predict outcome or other patient-related events

correct_answer.text: The validity of diagnosis cannot be assessed by comparison with a gold standard

correct_answers.text: The validity of diagnosis cannot be assessed by comparison with a gold standard

questions.explanation: The validity of a diagnosis describes the extent to which it corresponds to a gold standard and can be assessed in comparison with a gold standard.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not true regarding the sensitivity and specificity of an instrument?

options.text: The sensitivity of an instrument is the probability of diagnosing a disease when present
The specificity of an instrument is the probability of not diagnosing a disease when present
It is not possible for an instrument to be highly sensitive and highly specific
Sensitivity increases as the threshold for making the diagnosis is lowered
The specificity reduces as the threshold for making the diagnosis is lowered

correct_answer.text: The specificity of an instrument is the probability of not diagnosing a disease when present

correct_answers.text: The specificity of an instrument is the probability of not diagnosing a disease when present

questions.explanation: The specificity is the probability of not diagnosing disease when it is absent.

questions.question_text: Regarding the epidemiology of schizophrenia, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: Incidence is between 15 and 30 new cases per 100 000
Point prevalence is approximately 1%
Lifetime risk is approximately 1%
Age of onset is earlier in men than women
It is more common in males than females

correct_answer.text: It is more common in males than females

correct_answers.text: It is more common in males than females

questions.explanation: Schizophrenia is equally common in males and females.

questions.question_text: Regarding the epidemiology of schizophrenia, which of the following statements is true?

options.text: Rates from urban areas are usually lower than those from rural areas
According to social drift theory, women are more likely to drift into inner-city areas
Social residue theory explains that healthy people migrate away from undesirable areas, leaving schizophrenics behind
Breeder hypothesis rejects environmental factors of aetiological importance in schizophrenia
There is a higher incidence in those who have married

correct_answer.text: Social residue theory explains that healthy people migrate away from undesirable areas, leaving schizophrenics behind

correct_answers.text: Social residue theory explains that healthy people migrate away from undesirable areas, leaving schizophrenics behind

questions.explanation: In schizophrenia, the rates from urban areas are usually higher than those from rural areas. According to social drift theory (Goldberg & Morrison 1963) men are more likely to drift into inner-city areas. Breeder hypothesis (social causation hypothesis by Castle et al. 1993) suggested that some environmental factors of aetiological importance in schizophrenia are more likely to affect those born into households of lower socioeconomic status and in the inner city.

questions.question_text: Regarding the epidemiology of delusional disorders, all of the following statements are correct according to Munro's (1991) observations, except:

options.text: The mean age of onset is lower in males
The sex ratio is equal
The probability of delusional disorders is increased if there is a family history of delusional disorder and schizophrenia
Introverted personalities with long-standing interpersonal difficulties are more likely to suffer from delusional disorders
Delusional disorders increase with high rates of marital breakdown

correct_answer.text: The probability of delusional disorders is increased if there is a family history of delusional disorder and schizophrenia

correct_answers.text: The probability of delusional disorders is increased if there is a family history of delusional disorder and schizophrenia

questions.explanation: The probability of psychiatric disorder is increased if there is a family history of psychiatric disorder, but not likewise for delusional disorder and schizophrenia.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true regarding depressive disorder?

options.text: It is more common in females in all age groups
The point prevalence is higher in men
The average age of onset is around the late thirties
The incidence is lower in those who are unmarried
There is a higher prevalence in middle-class than in working-class women

correct_answer.text: The average age of onset is around the late thirties

correct_answers.text: The average age of onset is around the late thirties

questions.explanation: Depressive disorder is more common in females generally but male first admissions continue to climb until the end of life, overtaking female first admissions at the age of 85. The point prevalence is higher in women.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true regarding bipolar mood disorder?

options.text: The sex ratio is equal
The average age of onset is around the mid-twenties
It is more common in the upper social class
The point prevalence is between 0.4% and 1.25% in the adult population
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: Lifetime risk in the general population is 0.6–1.1%.

questions.question_text: Suicide is more common in:

options.text: Men
People aged over 45
Divorced people
Social classes 1 and 4
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: Suicide is also common in single and widowed people, and is associated with unemployment and retirement.

questions.question_text: Deliberate self-harm is more common in:

options.text: Females
Those aged below 35
Divorced and single people
Lower social class
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: Deliberate self-harm is also common in unemployed people and those living in overcrowded inner cities.

questions.question_text: In agoraphobias, there is a higher rate of comorbidity with:

options.text: Depression
Alcohol abuse
Simple phobia
Social phobia
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: There is a high degree of overlap in agoraphobia, simple phobia and social phobia. Individuals with major depression have a 9–15 times higher risk of developing agoraphobia and simple phobia.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements are true regarding the epidemiology of panic disorder, except:

options.text: It is twice as common in females as in males
Only the higher socioeconomic groups are affected
Onset is rare after the age of 40
It is more common in divorced people
A family history of panic disorder is associated with increased risk

correct_answer.text: Only the higher socioeconomic groups are affected

correct_answers.text: Only the higher socioeconomic groups are affected

questions.explanation: All socioeconomic groups are affected.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements are true regarding the epidemiology of generalized anxiety disorder (GAD), except:

options.text: Age of onset is earlier than in other anxiety disorders
Early-onset GAD is more likely in males
Early-onset GAD is associated with childhood fears
Early-onset GAD is associated with marital and sexual dysfunction
Late-onset GAD is more associated with stressful life events

correct_answer.text: Early-onset GAD is more likely in males

correct_answers.text: Early-onset GAD is more likely in males

questions.explanation: Early-onset generalized anxiety disorder (GAD) is more likely in females.

questions.question_text: Regarding the epidemiology of obsessive compulsive disorder, which of the following statements is true?

options.text: It is very rare in children
The sex ratio is equal
There is a bimodal age of onset
There is a decline in onset after the age of 35
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: There is a bimodal age of onset, with peaks occurring at ages 12–14 and 20–22 years.

questions.question_text: Regarding cyclical premenstrual symptoms, which of the following statements is true?

options.text: There is a higher prevalence in those around the age of 30 years
Prevalence decreases with increasing parity
There is a higher prevalence in women whose cycles are modified with oral contraceptive pills
There is a higher prevalence in women whose cycles are interrupted with pregnancy
All of the above

correct_answer.text: There is a higher prevalence in those around the age of 30 years

correct_answers.text: There is a higher prevalence in those around the age of 30 years

questions.explanation: Prevalence increases with increasing parity; there is a higher prevalence in those women who have experienced natural menstrual cycles for a longer period of time (whose cycles are not modified with oral contraceptive pills and are uninterrupted with pregnancy).

questions.question_text: All of the following factors are associated with women who develop puerperal psychosis, except:

options.text: Increased rate of caesarean section
Lower social class
Older age at birth of first child
Primiparae
Previous history of manic depressive illness

correct_answer.text: Lower social class

correct_answers.text: Lower social class

questions.explanation: Puerperal psychosis is more associated with higher social class.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements regarding anorexia nervosa are true, except:

options.text: It is rare, with a prevalence of one to two per 1000 women
Peak age is 15–19 years
There is a higher prevalence in higher socioeconomic classes
There is a significant association with lower parental education
Incidence is 10 times higher in females than in males

correct_answer.text: There is a significant association with lower parental education

correct_answers.text: There is a significant association with lower parental education

questions.explanation: There is a significant association with higher parental education, and it is higher in ballet and modelling schools.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true regarding bulimia?

options.text: Its prevalence may be slightly higher than that of anorexia
Social class distribution is more even than in anorexia
The age of onset is slightly higher than that of anorexia
The female to male ratio is 10:1
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: The prevalence of bulimia in adolescent and young adult females is approximately 1–3%.

questions.question_text: Which of the following psychiatric morbidities has the highest prevalence among those aged over 65?

options.text: Dementia
Depression
Phobic disorders
Paranoid states
Personality disorders

correct_answer.text: Depression

correct_answers.text: Depression

questions.explanation: The prevalence of dementia is 5%, depression 13.5%, phobic disorders 10%, paranoid states 0.5%, and personality disorders 1%. The prevalence of dementia rises with age, doubling every 5.1 years until in the over-80s it is 20%.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true of Huntington's disease?

options.text: It is autosomal dominant and fully penetrant
It affects 50% of offspring
There are five cases per 100 000 in the UK
Onset is usually between the ages of 35 and 45 years
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: Onset of Huntington's disease occurs in childhood in 10–20% of cases.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true regarding late-onset psychosis?

options.text: It is more common in females
46% have at least one Schneiderian first-rank symptom
The annual incidence is 17–26 per 100 000
It is associated with a lower rate of marriage and low fecundity
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: There is an increased risk of schizophrenia in first-degree relatives but the association is less than when compared with younger-onset schizophrenia.
